I am seventy years old and this is only my second year managing the farm myself, though I helped my father when I was a boy. I never went to school, so I cannot read the writing on the fertilizer bags or the papers from the seed shop. I watch what my neighbors do, especially Lao Zhang who has farmed this village for over thirty years, and I ask my son to read things for me when he visits from the factory in the county town. Our family has seven people, but two of my grandchildren work off-farm and are not here to help at busy times. We have six mu of land, which is not much, and I must be careful with every yuan.

Last year I put three mu into wheat and then maize on the same plot, two mu into cotton, and one mu into stevia because a buyer came to the village promising a good price. The wheat gave me about 350 kg per mu, the maize about 380 kg, the cotton about 220 kg of lint, and the stevia about 180 kg of dried leaves. It was enough to feed us and sell some, but not a great year. This year I will do almost the same because I am still learning, and changing too fast is dangerous for an old man with little experience.

For the wheat on three mu, I will rotary till in early October and sow the improved seed that Lao Zhang uses. I will put down one 50 kg bag of compound fertilizer and half a bag of urea per mu at planting, and if the wheat looks yellow after winter I will spread a little more urea. I will irrigate three times from my well: before freeze-up, at jointing, and when the grain is filling. Three sprays should be enough — one for weeds and two for bugs if I see aphids.

For maize on the same three mu, there is no time to till after harvesting wheat in early June. I will plant the hybrid maize seed directly into the wheat stubble, no-tillage, because if I wait the season will be too short. I will put compound fertilizer and some urea in the planting holes. Two irrigations should be enough if it rains, one in July and one in August. Two sprays: herbicide and one for corn borer.

For cotton on two mu, I will rotary till in April and plant the improved seed. Cotton needs many sprays — last year I sprayed ten or eleven times for bollworm and aphids, and I will do the same this year because the bugs never rest. Two irrigations, one at flowering and one when the bolls are growing. One bag of compound and some urea per mu, about the same as the wheat.

For stevia on one mu, I will till in spring and plant the improved seedlings. The neighbor who grows stevia told me it drinks a lot of water, so I will irrigate five times. Six sprays for weeds, insects, and the leaf spots that came last year. I expect about 180 kg per mu again, maybe a bit less if the soil is tired. I keep this crop because the buyer pays cash, and cash is what we need.
